patch_description:
The prior approach used a greedy multi-source attachment rule: at each iteration it selected the currently cheapest destination branch and attached it to the partially built tree. Its key parameters were implicit: edge `cost` was the sole optimization weight, all `num_partitions` were duplicated over the same route, and destination selection was based only on immediate incremental path cost. This can miss globally cheaper shared relay structures.

The new algorithm uses an exact directed Steiner-tree dynamic program when the number of unique destinations is at most `EXACT_TERMINAL_LIMIT = 11`. It minimizes the total cost of the union of broadcast links, allowing destinations to share low-cost prefixes and intermediate relay networks. The dynamic program evaluates all terminal subsets, merges compatible subtrees, and relaxes routes through the directed cloud graph. For larger destination sets, it uses a scalable shared-tree greedy fallback with terminal-leaf pruning. Paths are then extracted from the selected shared topology and replicated across partitions, preserving the original input/output interface.
